declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes and before any candidate run of these bytes. The shapes reduce the crate record after census 8's (core's `impl<I, U> Iterator for Flatten<I> where I: Iterator<Item: IntoIterator<IntoIter = U, Item = U::Item>>, U: Iterator` and its `fn next(&mut self) -> Option<U::Item>` at iter/adapters/flatten.rs). Analysis-only drafts of the first three shapes in obj/parallel/census-batch8/repro (flatten.rs, r-ret-noself.rs, r-fn-ret.rs) were run through rustc 1.98.0 and this compiler before this declaration, so those three are a regression record of that exploration; the two relaxed shapes were not. Each outcome follows the stated rule (a rigid projection proves a sizing goal from its associated type's own item bounds, whether declared `Sized` or implicitly `MetaSized` for `?Sized`, even when the environment holds sizing assumptions over other projections)

flatten-next.rs.reason: core's Flatten Iterator impl shape: `Option<U::Item>` needs the default `Sized` of `Iterator::Item` while the environment assumes `<I as Iterator>::Item: MetaSized`

inherent-item.rs.reason: the same `Option<U::Item>` in an inherent associated function of that impl

free-item.rs.reason: the same `Option<U::Item>` in a free function with the same where-clause

relaxed-meta.rs.reason: with `?Sized` items, `U::Item` is a `MetaSized` argument from its implicit `MetaSized` item bound
